title: Is the protection of birth beside the parent carried by genes clustering in space?
question: Over ten studies, populations whose newborns start beside a random stranger went extinct in 110/120 runs, against 43/120 beside the parent. Every ecological account tested has failed: local density, any relative, parental culling, the aggression sink, parent-offspring sharing, sensing the parent, and birth-site quality. An evolutionary account remains, from population genetics: when newborns start beside their parent, each family's genome stays clustered in space, so families compete as units and selection can act at the family level (multilevel selection in a viscous population). This study keeps newborns beside their parent but gives them the genome of a random unrelated agent, which breaks the link between where genes are and who carries them.
background: foster_genome=True: the newborn is placed beside its parent as usual, keeps its parent as its genealogical parent, but inherits the input weights and the aggression gene of a random living agent unrelated to its parent (mutated as usual). If no unrelated agent is alive, the parent's genome is used (counted in birth_fallback_frac). Interpretation rule, fixed in advance: the protection works through genomes clustering in space if H55a or H55b is supported; if neither, it does not depend on who carries which genes beside the parent. No pilot was run. Seeds 2900-2911 have never been run.

hypotheses.statement: With foster genomes, populations beside the parent go extinct more often
With foster genomes, populations beside the parent die out sooner
Foster-genome populations differ in extinction from stranger populations
